new_roles.description:
**Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.**

### **Job Description:**

Director, Executive Protection, Protective Operations and Logistics

The Role:

As the Director of Protective Operations and Logistics within the Executive Protection team, you will be responsible for executive protection program management and logistical planning, including staffing, scheduling*,* protective transportation operations, support request vetting and assessment, training administration, and oversight of the TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program. Reporting to the Head of Executive Protection, you will provide operational leadership, program oversight, and subject matter expertise on executive protection and protective operations matters. You willbe responsible for ensuring the effective execution of day-to-day protective operations while supporting the continued enhancement of the firm's executive protection capabilities. The position requires close collaboration with Global Security Operations, the Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), Travel Security, and key internal and external partners to implement and support Fidelity's executive protection strategy. Success in this role requires exceptional organizational, leadership, and relationship-management skills, as well as the ability to balance competing priorities while delivering consistent, discreet, and service-oriented experience for Fidelity's senior leadership.

The Expertise and Skills You Bring

* 7-10 years of experience protecting C-suite executives, board members, and/or government officials in complex, dynamic, and globally distributed operating environments within corporate, government, military, or law enforcement settings.
* Exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple workstreams
* Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with executives, business leaders, security professionals, and external stakeholders
* Extensive knowledge of executive protection operations, including protective advances, travel security, transportation security, venue assessment, route planning and protective operations logistics.
* Expertise in assessing, prioritizing, and coordinating executive support requests while balancing risk, resource requirements, and business priorities.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required and operate effectively in dynamic, rapidly changing, and high-pressure environments.
* Strong understanding of TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program requirements, administration, compliance, certifications, and operational integration; the ability to obtain and maintain ASO certification is highly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to manage executive protection staffing models, personnel scheduling, resource allocation, and operational readiness across multiple locations and priorities.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, develop, and build high-performing teams while fostering a culture of professionalism, accountability, discretion, and service excellence.
* Experience coordinating and supporting executive travel, special events, corporate meetings, and other high-visibility engagements requiring detailed planning and collaboration.
* Experience managing executive transportation programs, including vehicle operations, driver standards, fleet utilization, and transportation security protocols.
* Experience developing and managing executive protection training programs, operational exercises, performance standards, readiness assessments, and professional development initiatives.
* Bachelor's degree is preferred; equivalent professional experience will be considered.
* Relevant professional certifications such as CTM, CPP, PSP, ASIS Executive Protection Professional (EPP), TSA ASO, or other intelligence, investigation, or executive protection credentials are a plus.
* undefined

The Purpose of Your Role

 

* Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of executive protection programs that ensure the safety, privacy, and operational effectiveness of Fidelity's executive leadership.
* Manage the day-to-day administration and logistical support of executive protection operations, including staffing, scheduling, executive travel, protective transportation, training, and resource allocation.
* Provide operational leadership and oversight for executive protection program management, ensuring consistent service delivery, operational readiness, and alignment with organizational priorities.
* Serve as a trusted partner to executive stakeholders by delivering responsive, discreet, and customer-focused protective services in support of business activities and executive requirements.
* Oversee the planning and coordination of executive travel, special events, site visits, and high-profile engagements, ensuring appropriate protective measures and logistical support are in place.
* Manage and enhance the TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program, executive transportation services, training initiatives, and other core executive protection capabilities.
* Serve as a trusted security advisor to senior executives, providing strategic guidance, risk-based recommendations, and executive-level briefings on protective operations, emerging threats, and security-related matters.

The Team

The Executive Protection team is part of the broader Protective Services team, which in turn is part of Fidelity’s Global Security team. The Executive Protection team is a highly valued team dedicated to the protection of the firm’s executive leadership and events.

Please be advised that Fidelity’s business is governed by the provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, ERISA, numerous state laws governing securities, investment and retirement-related financial activities and the rules and regulations of numerous self-regulatory organizations, including FINRA, among others. Those laws and regulations may restrict Fidelity from hiring and/or associating with individuals with certain Criminal Histories.

Fidelity’s Onsite Working Model 
Fidelity is transitioning to a full-time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles.

The base salary range for this position is $95,000-186,000 USD per year.

Placement in the range will vary based on job responsibilities and scope, geographic location, candidate’s relevant experience, and other factors.

Base salary is only part of the total compensation package. Depending on the position and eligibility requirements, the offer package may also include bonus or other variable compensation.

We offer a wide range of benefits to meet your evolving needs and help you live your best life at work and at home. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage and emotional well-being support, market-leading retirement, generous paid time off and parental leave, charitable giving employee match program, and educational assistance including student loan repayment, tuition reimbursement, and learning resources to develop your career. Note, the application window closes when the position is filled or unposted.

Please be advised that Fidelity’s business is governed by the provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, ERISA, numerous state laws governing securities, investment and retirement-related financial activities and the rules and regulations of numerous self-regulatory organizations, including FINRA, among others. **About Southern Brew** 
At 7 Brew, we serve more than just coffee - we're brewing connection, culture, and community at high speed. Every stand is built on energy, authenticity, and exceptional service. 
Southern Brew operates more than 80 stands and is rapidly expanding its 7 Brew portfolio, with plans to become one of the largest 7 Brew franchisees in the country over the next five years. 
 
We're looking for a **Director of Operations** to help lead that growth. 
 
**The Role** 
As Director of Operations, you'll lead and develop Regional Managers while driving operational excellence, financial performance, talent development, and successful new stand openings across your market. 
You'll be responsible for turning company goals into results while building strong leaders and ensuring every stand delivers the culture and experience 7 Brew is known for.

new_roles.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION** 
 
 

Step into a leadership role, where your management skills will drive strategic risk and compliance initiatives. Embrace the opportunity to enhance your leadership capabilities and make a meaningful impact on the future of risk management and control testing. 
 
As a **Compliance and Operations Risk Test Director** in the Testing Center of Excellence, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the testing strategy across various business lines, ensuring alignment with regulatory and firm requirements. Your expertise in risk management and control testing will be instrumental in identifying and mitigating risks, thereby enhancing compliance and operational risk management. You will be expected to make independent decisions that significantly impact operations and financial management, while also leading large teams and managing service delivery. Your proficiency in problem-solving, decision-making, and resource optimization will be key in driving results that accelerate our business objectives. Your role will also involve fostering strong relationships with stakeholders, interpreting regulatory requirements, and effectively communicating risk reports to various management levels. 
 
**Job responsibilities**

* Lead the development and implementation of comprehensive testing strategies across various business lines, ensuring alignment with regulatory and firm requirements.
* Oversee complex testing initiatives, utilizing advanced knowledge in risk management and control testing to identify and mitigate unmitigated risks.
* Make independent, strategic decisions that significantly impact operations, financial management, and compliance, based on in-depth analysis and expert judgment.
* Foster strong relationships with senior stakeholders, interpreting regulatory requirements and effectively communicating risk reports to various management levels.
* Manage large teams, setting professional standards, and ensuring efficient service delivery, while also contributing to the longer-term plans for the area to fit within broader functional and organization strategy.

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* 10 years of experience in leading and implementing comprehensive testing strategies in a financial institution.
* Proven track record in managing large teams, setting professional standards, and ensuring efficient service delivery.
* Demonstrated expertise in interpreting and applying regulatory requirements within the context of risk management and control testing.
* Advanced proficiency in utilizing risk dashboards to provide SMART risk reporting, communications, and presentations for various forums and management levels.
* Expertise in resource optimization, with a focus on efficiently leveraging allocated people, money, and technologies to plan, schedule, and progress project and program initiatives.

**ABOUT US** 
 
 

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

new_roles.title: Director, Operational Excellence and Innovation
new_roles.description:
**Job Overview**

Citadel Credit Union is seeking a visionary leader to serve as Director of Operational Excellence & Innovation. This role will drive process improvement within the Experience & Retail team and will focus on enhancing current business processes within the team. This position will also focus on integrating new technologies within the organization, such as blockchain (DLT), smart contracts, and artificial intelligence into member and employee experience to drive efficiency, automation and service improvements. The Director will lead, collaborate, and influence the business to modernize workflows, automate processes, and position Citadel as a technology leader in retail financial services.

**What will I be doing?**

As a Director of Operational Excellence & Innovation, you will support Citadel’s Experience and Retail environments in meeting strategic initiatives for our members. The following tasks must be executed with high fidelity:

* Lead the design and implementation of emerging technologies to include blockchain and AI-powered automation solutions for retail operations.
* Act as liaison and collaborate with various lines of business, including EPMO, Digital & Transformation, and Retail Operations & Support.
* Coordinating of testing and implementing branch technology and compliance.
* Act as liaison between the team and internal/external partners to ensure successful deployment of system upgrades and enhancements.
* Manage team related vendor relationships.
* Oversee the development and deployment of smart contracts to automate efficiencies in member onboarding, KYC/AML/NRA compliance, transaction processing, and reporting.
* Identify, assess, and recommend blockchain platforms, smart contract frameworks, and AI vendors to support retail automation initiatives.
* Collaborates on system and workflow enhancements while acting as a vendor and system liaison.
* Manage pilot programs for new automation solutions, collect feedback, refine processes, and oversee full-scale deployment and staff training across team channels.
* Ensure all solutions meet regulatory requirements, maintain data immutability, and enhance fraud prevention through biometric and cryptographic security.
* Monitor system performance, optimize retail workflows, and implement enhancements based on analytics and stakeholder input.
* Develop and execute strategies to overcome resistance to technology adoption, including comprehensive staff training and phased implementation.

**What we are looking for?**

* 7+ years’ experience in process improvement, project management, or technology implementation in retail financial services.
* Bachelor's degree; MBA or advanced degree a plus
* Proven expertise in blockchain/DLT, smart contracts, and AI workflow automation.
* Strong understanding of KYC/AML/NRA compliance and regulatory reporting in retail banking.
* Experience with vendor selection and management for enterprise technology solutions.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to analyze complex retail workflows and drive cross-functional collaboration.
* Familiarity with zero-trust architecture and Microsoft Azure AD integration.
* Experience with RPA tools and business process automation platforms.
* Knowledge of UTAUT, TPB, and TAM models for user technology adoption.
* Prior experience in retail financial technology innovation or credit union operations.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality Operations
existing_roles.description:
At Keros, our mission is to deliver significant clinical benefit to a wide range of patients with disorders that are linked to dysfunctional signaling of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-ß) family of proteins. With a focus on developing differentiated product candidates that are designed to alter TGF-β signaling, we aim to target the pathways critical for the growth, repair and maintenance of blood cells and a number of tissues, including bone, skeletal muscle, adipose and heart tissue. We believe our product candidates have the potential to unlock the full therapeutic benefits of modulating the TGF-β superfamily and provide disease-modifying benefit to patients.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Director of Quality Operations is responsible for providing quality oversight to all manufacturing operations in support of clinical development and commercial products, including but not limited to, Drug substance, Process Intermediates, and Drug Product(s). This role requires extensive interaction with Clinical Operations, Pharmaceutical Operations, Program and CMC project management, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and CMOs, to achieve sustainable compliance in GxP operations.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide quality oversight to all manufacturing operations in support of clinical development and commercial products. Ensure all manufacturing activities in support of Drug substance, Process Intermediates, and Drug Product(s), are conducted in accordance with internal company standards and in compliance with quality agreements.
* Formulating and administering policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) relating to the Quality Operations function and quality management system identifying opportunities for improvements.
* Ownership of real time batch record review and resolution of associated deviations prior to product disposition.
* Quality oversight of Deviations, Change Controls, CAPAs, etc., including those at the CMO sites.
* Developing and implementing appropriate quality training for the team.
* Assuring availability of all required documentation and support for the Annual Product Reviews
* Review of CMC sections for regulatory submissions to ensure accuracy and completeness. Participate in activities to assist with regulatory submissions, control strategy development and CMC strategy.
* Quality review and approval of Technology transfer protocols and final reports.
* Preparation for regulatory inspections at the CMO sites.
* Define, develop, and implement short-term and long-term strategies, goals, objectives, and tactics relating to the Quality Operations function and the quality management system.
* Review and recommend appropriate corrective action to ensure consistency with the Quality Operations function and the quality management system.
* Using incident and Corrective and Preventive Action ("CAPA") activities and processes to drive quality improvements and respond to process and service issues.
* Represent Quality Operations function and quality management system and related processes in connection with internal or external audits, inspections, monitoring visits and new business development activities, and assist with quality-related information related to (but not limited to) client assessments, RFPs, contracts, and other documentation.
* Assist Keros Quality Systems & Compliance team to perform GMP audits for vendors; follow through remediation plans assigned from audit observations and ensure internal and external CAPAs are completed within the mandated timelines.
* Maintain current knowledge base of regulations, corporate policies, and standards to ensure that the Quality Operations function remain in compliance with applicable regulatory and corporate standards/requirements and current with industry trends and best practices.
* Support strategic planning by timely communicating Quality deliverables, constraints, risks, and options, and collaborating with Technical Development, Program management, Clinical, Commercial, Supply Chain, and internal and external Manufacturing teams.
* Identify risks and assumptions in plans, anticipate problems and plan for contingencies. Remove obstacles to move work forward and/or to get efforts back on track. Work effectively in team to help issue resolution. Ability to provide phase specific guidance from quality perspective, and to prioritize and multitask as necessary.
* Manage and mentor Quality operations staff to emphasize positional responsibilities, and personnel development. Must be able to coach and mentor quality personnel in necessary skills to review and approve highly technical documentation.
* Any additional duties assigned by supervisor.

**Qualifications**

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree is required (Biological sciences, Engineering, or related degree); advanced degree is a plus.
* Minimum of 12 years CGMP Quality experience in the Pharmaceutical/Biopharmaceutical/ Biotechnology industry.
* Ideally a minimum of 8 years of experience in leading a Quality function.
* Ideally a minimum of 3 years of experience at the Director level with successfully managing direct reports.
* Strong knowledge of biological manufacturing process and testing.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Proven ability to effectively develop, communicate, and gain support for execution plans and strategies with a wide range of stakeholders.
* Leadership and management skills to grow and manage a high performing Quality organization.
* Demonstrated skills in project management and working with vendors and contractors.
* Strong understanding of FDA, ISO, EMA, GMP and ICH requirements ideally for ATMPs.
* Proven experience with regulatory submissions, ideally for products which were ultimately approved for commercial distribution, and regulatory inspections.
* Excellent judgment and creative problem-solving skills, including negotiation and conflict resolution skills, excellent interpersonal skills, organizational skills, written and oral communication skills.
* Experience developing and executing organizational change, including change management strategy and planning.
* Energetic, flexible, collaborative, and proactive; a leader who can positively and productively impact initiatives.
* Available to work in the evenings and weekends if required.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Our Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Mission Statement:**Keros is an inclusive company. We believe that diversity drives innovation. We continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices of our employees. As such, Keros takes a holistic approach in mentoring, coaching, and developing all of our Keros team members.

*Keros Therapeutics is an Equal Opportunity employer. **Description:**

The Director, Quality – External Manufacturing leads the External Quality team responsible for quality oversight of Amneal's network of 50+ external manufacturers, including contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs), contract packagers, contract testing laboratories, and API/critical material suppliers across oral solid dose, injectables, and complex products. The role ensures that products manufactured or tested externally meet Amneal's quality standards, approved regulatory filings, and applicable cGMP requirements, and that Amneal's Quality Unit retains full accountability for outsourced operations. Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Quality, the Director leads a team of External Quality Managers and QA Leads, each accountable for a defined set of partners / activities, and works closely with Supply Chain, Procurement, Research & Development, and Regulatory Affairs.

**Essential Functions:**

* External Quality Leadership & Network Oversight - Lead quality oversight of 50+ external manufacturers, contract laboratories, and business partners. Establish a risk-based oversight model that tiers partners by product criticality, dosage form, regulatory history, and performance, and sets audit frequency, on-site presence, and review depth accordingly. Serve as the senior Quality decisionmaker for external manufacturing issues, product impact assessments, and escalations. Represent External Quality in management review and Quality Council forums.
* People Leadership - Lead, coach, and develop a team of External Quality Managers and QA Leads; assign partner portfolios and balance workload across 50+ sites. Build team capability in auditing, investigation review, risk assessment, and regulatory requirements. Develop and maintain SOPs, tools, and standard work for external quality oversight. Foster a culture of quality ownership, independent challenge, transparency, and continuous improvement.
* Quality Agreements & Partner Qualification – Own the authoring, negotiation, approval, and periodic review of Quality Agreements. Lead quality due diligence, qualification, and approval of new partners; maintain the Approved Supplier List. Define and execute the CMO and contract laboratory audit program; ensure audit observations are tracked to effective closure. Lead quality disqualification and exit decisions for persistently non-compliant partners.
* Batch Disposition & Product Quality - Ensure timely, compliant review and disposition of externally manufactured batches against approved specifications and registered processes. Oversee review of executed batch records, CoAs, and release testing performed at contract laboratories. Ensure Annual Product Reviews incorporate complete and accurate CMO data and drive actions from trends. Oversee stability program commitments, OOS/OOT trending, and product quality complaints for externally manufactured products.
* Deviations, Investigations & CAPA - Ensure deviations, OOS/OOT results, and complaints at partner sites are investigated thoroughly and in a timely manner. Challenge root cause analyses for scientific rigor and identification of systemic contributors. Approve CAPAs and verify effectiveness; identify recurring issues across partners and drive network-wide preventive actions. Lead quality assessments for field alerts, recalls, and market actions involving external products.
Change Control & Regulatory Alignment - Govern partner-initiated and Amneal-initiated changes through change control, including product impact and regulatory reportability assessments. Partner with Regulatory Affairs to ensure changes are filed appropriately (CBE-0, CBE-30, PAS, annual report) and that partner operations remain aligned with approved ANDAs/NDAs. Provide quality oversight of technology transfers, site transfers, process validation, and new product launches at external sites.  

This position requires 30-40% travel both domestic and international.

  

**Education:**

* Bachelor's Degree (BA/BS) Chemistry, biology, Pharmacy, engineering or other technical fields - Required
Master's degree (MS/MA) Chemistry, biology, Pharmacy, engineering or other technical fields - Preferred  

**Experience:**

* 15 years or more in QA, QC, Compliance in pharmaceutical manufacturing company.
* 5 years or more in External / CMO quality oversight.
Must have experience managing others.  

**Specialized Knowledge:**

* Demonstrated quality oversight of a large, multi-site CMO network across dosage forms (oral solids, sterile injectables, and/or complex generics).
* Expert knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210/211, 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP, ICH Q7/Q9/Q10, and FDA expectations for Quality Agreements and outsourced manufacturing.
* Experience hosting or supporting FDA inspections and leading 483 / Warning Letter remediation.
Strong background in investigations, root cause analysis, CAPA, and change control.

The Director of Enterprise Quality & Assurance will establish and lead the Enterprise Quality Management function under the Enterprise Risk & Compliance organization, providing an enterprise-wide framework to strengthen quality, promote consistent execution, and drive continuous improvement to PG&E’s Layers of Defense framework. Accountable for applying risk-informed assurance activities to increase confidence that operational processes and controls are effective and deliver intended safety, quality, compliance, and business outcomes. Plans, organizes, and directs assurance and quality management activities, leading staff and partnering with functional area coworkers to support PG&E’s collective success.

This position reports to the Senior Director, Enterprise Assurance and will lead a team of 4 quality assurance professionals, both full-time employees and contractors. The Director will build the team as needed.

Leads risk-informed assurance activities to increase confidence in operational process performance and risk management, with an initial focus on the Power Generation line of business. Strong analytical and risk assessment skills

* Serve as the primary site subject matter expert during regulatory inspections and customer audits involving laboratory operations and quality systems.

* Lead laboratory optimization, method modernization, automation, Lean deployment, and quality system improvement initiatives.

**What sets you up for success:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline required; master’s degree or doctorate preferred.
* 10+ years of related experience, including significant leadership responsibility within laboratory quality control or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Demonstrated expertise in QC Chemistry and/or QC Microbiology operations within a sterile drug product manufacturing environment.
* Significant experience with laboratory compliance, data integrity, out-of-specification and out-of-trend investigations, analytical methods, and pharmaceutical quality systems.
* Proven experience supporting regulatory inspections, customer audits, and interactions with senior internal and external stakeholders.
* Ability to resolve complex scientific, operational, and compliance issues using sound judgment, technical expertise, and risk-based decision-making.

**What you will enjoy along the way:**

* The opportunity to shape the laboratory quality strategy for a regulated sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site.

Job Description
  
  
Position Overview
  
  
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical
  
Global Quality Management Systems
  
  
The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.
  
  
This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.
  
  
The QMS Quality Lead will oversee the harmonization and evolution of quality processes—including deviation management, investigations, CAPA, change control, risk management (ICH Q9), and computerized systems validation (CSV/CSA)—to ensure seamless integration with modern automated laboratory workflows, LIMS, ELN, and digital data pipelines. In close partnership with the program leadership team, Site Quality heads, Analytical Development, Digital/IT Quality, and Regulatory Compliance, the incumbent will ensure that innovative operational models maintain rigorous compliance with global health authority regulations while driving efficiency, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Key Responsibilities and Requirements
  
The ideal candidate will combine deep technical expertise in global Quality Management Systems with a forward-thinking innovation mindset, translating digital and automated laboratory advancements into agile, compliant, and sustainable QMS frameworks.
  
  

* Strategic QMS Architecture & Modernization: Define, lead, and execute the QMS integration strategy for the lab transformation initiative, ensuring core quality processes (Change Control, OOS/OOE/OOT investigations, Deviations, CAPA, Method Transfer/Validation, and Batch Release support) are optimized, digitized, and natively integrated with automated laboratory systems
* Coding Experience: Experience and understanding on how coding translates to QMS and analytical functions. Responsible for overseeing the eQMS and ability to be able to review and understand the underlying code and how it is ensures compliance.
* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.
* Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness: Ensure all modernized QMS processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) comply with global cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Part 11/210/211, EU Annex 11, ICH Q9/Q10, WHO). Drive inspection readiness strategies and author/review corresponding regulatory briefing documents and filing sections.
* Matrixed Program Leadership & Governance: Direct the QMS workstream governance forum, actively tracking milestone execution, interdependencies, risks, and critical paths. Provide regular data-driven progress updates, risk assessments, and escalation pathways to the Overall Quality Lead and executive steering bodies.
* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the central quality authority across laboratory operations, technology development, computerized systems validation, and regulatory affairs, eliminating silos and resolving complex compliance roadblocks.
* People Leadership & Oversight: Supervise and mentor quality specialists, compliance leads, and external consultants supporting QMS transformation, maintaining high standards of technical rigor, accountability, and development.

Required Experience
  
  

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacy, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related discipline required; advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD, or MBA) strongly preferred.
* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
* Quality Systems Expertise: Proven track record in designing, optimizing, and overseeing enterprise-level QMS processes (Deviations, Investigations, CAPA, Change Control, Out of Specification, and Quality Risk Management) in laboratories subject to global health authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).
* Digital & Laboratory Systems Acumen: In-depth knowledge of laboratory digital ecosystems, including LIMS, ELN, CDS, SDMS, automated instrumentation, and their integration into enterprise QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva Vault QMS).
* Validation & Compliance Mastery: Strong understanding of Data Integrity expectations, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and modern risk-based validation methodologies (GAMP 5, Computer Software Assurance).
* Governance & Program Execution: Demonstrated success leading large-scale cross-functional workstreams, setting project milestones, proactively managing risk registers, and driving accountable execution.
* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

Preferred Experience
  
  

* Direct experience leading or supporting QMS transformation initiatives (e.g., transition from paper/hybrid to end-to-end digitized paperless QC environments).
* Working knowledge of automated testing platforms, robotics, or continuous manufacturing/testing control frameworks.
* Experience with global health authority inspections, pre-approval inspections (PAIs), and authoring QMS/Quality sections for regulatory dossiers (NDA, BLA, MAA).
* Practical application of Lean / Six Sigma methodologies to streamline quality workflows and cycle times.
* Programming experience is an asset, and or strong demonstrated ability to quickly learn.
* Experience supporting enterprise workforce strategy, technology evaluation, or transition initiatives.
* Experience managing external third party service providers, software vendors, and implementation partners in regulated environments.

**Required Skills:**  
Analytical Development, Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Transformation, Enterprise Transformation, Executive Communications, GMP Compliance, Laboratory Quality Control, Project Governance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Regulatory Strategies
  
  
**Preferred Skills:**  
Analytical Testing, Change Leadership, Program Governance

**Transforming Cancer Therapy Together**

At ADC Therapeutics, we are passionate about revolutionizing cancer treatment. When you join our team, you become part of a mission-driven group of talented individuals dedicated to making a difference in patients' lives.

**Why ADC Therapeutics?**

ADC Therapeutics (NYSE): is a commercial, global leader and pioneer in the field of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) with specialized capabilities from clinical through commercialization. Our CD-19-directed ADC for relapsed/refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma, ZYNLONTA® (loncastuxamab tesirine lpyl) has received accelerated approval in the United States, conditional approval from the European Commission and conditional approvals in other countries. ZYNLONTA is also being evaluated in combination with other agents and in earlier lines of DLBCL therapy as well as indolent lymphomas including follicular lymphoma and marginal zone lymphoma with the potential to reach significantly more patients through expanded use.

We are a team of approximately 150 patient-focused, purpose-driven employees with a shared mission to transform the treatment paradigm for patients. If you’re interested in making a difference in the lives of patients worldwide with a team of like-minded colleagues, operating in a flexible work environment, come join us on our journey! To learn more about ADC Therapeutics, our values, and our exceptional culture, please visit us at https://adctherapeutics.com/ and LinkedIn.

**Job Summary****:**

The Senior Director of Manufacturing Sciences & Technologies (MSAT) is a senior technical leader responsible for end-to-end process ownership, technical oversight, and lifecycle management of drug substance intermediates, ADC drug substance, and ADC drug product manufactured through a global network of external CDMOs.

This role ensures robust, scalable, and compliant manufacturing processes that support commercial manufacturing, process development projects and clinical development, while serving as the senior-level technical support for internal Production Management Teams and external manufacturing partners.

The position plays a critical role in process validation, technology transfer, continued process verification (CPV), change management, technical and regulatory support across antibody, linker-payload, conjugation, formulation, fill/finish, and packaging operations.

This position reports to the Vice President, Global Supply & Operations. The role is remote based, with a preference for candidates located on the U.S. East Coast.

**What You'll Do****:**

MSAT Strategy and Leadership

* Lead and develop the MSAT function covering ADC end-to-end manufacturing across clinical and commercial stages.
* Define MSAT strategy for external manufacturing aligned with corporate objectives.

The Director, Digital Twin & Intelligent Manufacturing Capabilities is responsible for defining and advancing the enterprise strategy, technology direction, governance, standards, and capability roadmap for Digital Twins, Process Twins, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, Automation-enabled Manufacturing, and AI-driven manufacturing capabilities across Global Technical Operations (GTO). This is a multi-site position, initially focused on Jensen Metal Products and Jensen Powder Finishers. The successful candidate will build the structure, discipline, and performance culture needed to support long-term growth across KSP Group.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in fabrication and manufacturing environments, a strong operational and financial mindset, and a proven ability to lead teams through growth and transformation.

KSP Group is a family-owned organization with a diverse portfolio of manufacturing and consumer product companies

* **Jensen Metal Products** – Custom metal fabrication, welding, machining, laser cutting, engineering and contract manufacturing solutions (Racine, WI)
* **Jensen Powder Finishers** – Advanced powder coating and finishing services (Sturtevant, WI)

Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a visible impact, influence company strategy, and help shape the future of multiple growing businesses.

Executive Strategic & Business Leadership

* Identify opportunities for automation, process optimization, capacity expansion, and operational scalability

Financial & Operational Performance

* Own operational performance and P&L results across assigned manufacturing operations
* Develop departmental budgets, monitor spending, and ensure responsible management of operational resources
* Analyze manufacturing costs, labor efficiency, productivity metrics, and operating expenses to drive profitability
* Report on operational performance and improvement initiatives to executive leadership

Manufacturing Operations & Continuous Improvement

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives across fabrication, welding, machining, powder coating, assembly, engineering, and support functions
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, 5S, root cause problem solving, and waste reduction efforts
* Improve throughput, quality, safety, delivery performance, and overall operational efficiency
* Lead cross-functional projects focused on sustainable operational gains and measurable business results

Leadership & Culture

* Build, coach, and develop high-performing operational leadership teams
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement
* Promote employee engagement while creating a safe, quality-focused work environment

* Production planning and scheduling

* Quality improvement initiatives
* Corrective action processes

* Frontline leadership development

**Travel Requirements**

**About Us**

Jensen Metal Products is a metal fabrication business with over 100 years of experience serving the Midwest and surrounding regions with custom, quality sheet metal parts and assemblies. With a broad range of manufacturing capabilities, we produce a diverse portfolio of products, including our own line of fireplaces, which has been in production since 1970. At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We’re looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world.
  
  
Position Brand Description
  
How would you like a career where you get to apply your best technical and analytical skills to bring complex, high-potency biologic medicines to patients? We are seeking a scientific leader on our Parenteral Product Network Technical Services/Manufacturing Science (TS/MS) team to drive the commercialization of lyophilized drug products, with a focus on antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), and to provide technical support for commercial lyophilized product manufacturing.
  
In this role, you are critical to the success of Lilly’s oncology and biologics portfolio. As a Global Product Steward and lyophilization process expert, you will hold technical ownership of assigned lyophilized ADC and other parenteral products from late-stage development through the commercial lifecycle, serving as the technical link between Product Development and our commercial manufacturing sites. You will ensure these products are successfully launched, reliably supplied, and technically well controlled across internal and external sites.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
As an individual contributor, you will work side by side with colleagues in Product Development, Manufacturing Operations, Quality, EHS, and Supply Chain, as well as with external manufacturing organizations. You will be a visible technical presence in cross-functional teams, mentor junior technical associates, and escalate significant technical, quality, safety, and supply risks to management with clear assessments and recommended actions.
  
  
**Key responsibilities include:**  

* Serve as Global Product Steward and subject matter expert for lyophilized, ADC and parenteral products, holding end-to-end technical accountability for process performance, product quality, and supply across all manufacturing sites, and serving as the primary technical interface between Product Development and commercial manufacturing.
* Advance lyophilization technology in commercial manufacturing
* Maintain the product technical knowledge base and lifecycle strategy, including process history, critical material and supplier knowledge, a product technical risk register, and a roadmap for yield, robustness, capacity, and site-network improvements.
* Collaborate with product development and manufacturing site for technology transfer, scale-up, process performance qualification/validation, and comparability activities (including lyophilization cycle transfer between freeze-dryers of differing scale and design) to support commercial launch readiness.
* Escalate significant technical, quality, safety, compliance, and supply risks to TS/MS management in a timely manner, providing risk assessments, impact to patients and supply, and recommended mitigation plans.
* Own the commercial control strategy for lyophilization critical process parameters and critical quality attributes, and maintain process understanding through continued process verification, stability and batch trending, and global product assessment.
* Partner with Product Development to ensure manufacturability of new ADC and lyophilized products, and to provide commercial manufacturing feedback that informs formulation, cycle design, specifications, container closure selection, and site selection.
* Author and review technical sections of global regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and responses to regulatory questions, and support inspection readiness at commercial sites.
* Lead process improvement and lifecycle management projects, including introduction of new lyophilization, filling, and containment technologies and qualification of vials, stoppers, and other critical materials.

Basic Qualifications
  
  

* A degree in a relevant area such as Pharmaceutical Science, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry, or Chemistry with one of the following:
* PhD degree with 5 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Master’s degree with 10 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing, or
* Bachelor’s degree with 15 years of practical experience in parenteral, biologic, or antibody drug conjugate drug substance or drug product development and/or manufacturing.
* Hands-on experience with lyophilization development or manufacturing (e.g., formulation and cycle development, scale-up, tech transfer, or commercial cycle support).
* Working knowledge of protein-based and ADC drug product formulation and aseptic fill/finish processes.
* Experience supporting GMP commercial manufacturing, including technology transfer, process validation, and/or deviation investigation and resolution.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. Lilly does not anticipate providing sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B or TN status) for this employment position.
  
  
Additional Skills/Preferences
  
We want you to bring your lyophilization and biologics expertise, commercial manufacturing experience, and technical influence to help launch and supply ADC and other lyophilized medicines.
  
  
**Preferred experience includes:**  

* Direct ADC drug product experience, including handling of cytotoxic or highly potent payloads and the stability and process sensitivities of conjugated antibodies.
* Background in lyophilized product development, including formulation and excipient selection, freeze-drying cycle design, and thermal characterization, and cycle scale-up.
* Analytical characterization of lyophilized biologics and ADCs
* Experience with container closure and critical material qualification, including vial and stopper selection, container closure integrity, and the interaction of materials with processing equipment.
* Product stewardship experience, such as serving as technical owner or product lead for a commercial or late-stage product, authoring annual product reviews or technical risk assessments, and managing multi-site process harmonization.

existing_roles.description:
**Summary**
-----------

**This posting is open to all qualified candidates.**

  
  
  
  
Are you looking for an opportunity to lead a highly trained team of Operations and Maintenance (O&M) staff and be a part of creating the strategic direction for a complex wastewater system? The Wastewater Treatment Division (WTD) in King County (KC) is hiring a leader for the Brightwater Treatment Plant. This position will lead a team of 40 Operations, maintenance and Facilities staff, oversee the planning and processes for facilities maintenance of the Brightwater system, and be an active member of the O&M Leadership team.
  
  
Working for KC WTD provides you with a work-life balance and benefits to support you and your family. You will also gain opportunities for growth through training, conferences hosted by leaders in the industry, and working across functional groups within the Division.
  
  
We are looking for creative and innovative thinking that drives us to continuously improve public service. Tap into your desire to serve the public and discover new and better ways to make a meaningful impact by joining the WTD O&M Leadership team.
  
  
**About the Role:**
  
This is a leadership position and will serve on the Operations and Maintenance Section Leadership team. This team is responsible for the strategic planning of the section, developing leadership skills among our supervisors, providing growth opportunities for our staff, and implementing metrics to deliver key performance measures that contribute to the overall growth and success of WTD Operations and Maintenance.
  
  
In this role, the successful candidate will apply their skillset in the areas of planning, coordination, scope, budget, schedule management, monitoring and control, and reporting in the maintenance and development of the Brightwater Treatment System.
  
  
**About the Team:**
  
The Operations and Maintenance Section of the Wastewater Treatment Division is tasked with ensuring safe, environmentally protective wastewater treatment for King County, serving 34 wholesale customers and approximately 2.3 million residents. The Section includes five treatment facilities, 48 pump stations, 400 miles of conveyance piping and treats an average of 185MGD of wastewater. We are a clean water utility, recovering resources such as biosolids, recycled water and biogas, continually seeking new ways to capture beneficial uses of resources that would otherwise be lost.
  
  
WTD is committed to the principles of equity and social justice (ESJ). We value diverse perspectives and life experiences in our workforce and are committed to building a culturally diverse and inclusive environment. WTD strives to provide equitable services to residents and businesses across King County. Our department vision is to provide sustainable and livable communities and a clean and healthy natural environment that supports a prosperous and resilient economy.  
  
  

Join our team dedicated to ensuring clean water for generations to come! With over 1000 employees engaged in planning, designing, building, and operating treatment facilities, our agency is at the forefront of environmental stewardship. Success for us means upholding our legacy while promising future generations a pristine environment.

  
  

We partner with regulatory agencies to reduce harmful waste discharge and actively educate the public and businesses on water quality protection. We prioritize accountability to our ratepayers and operate a well-managed agency that services over 2.3 million King County residents. Our regional wastewater treatment system not only sustains a healthy environment but also fuels economic development, fostering prosperity in our region. If you're passionate about making a difference and thrive in a collaborative environment, join us in our mission to safeguard our precious water resources.

  
  

**Commitment to Equity, Racial and Social Justice:**

King County, named after Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., is a diverse and vibrant community that represents cultures from around the world. We prioritize equity, racial and social justice, making it a foundational and daily expectation for all employees. As a Wastewater Treatment Plant Manager, you will actively apply these principles in all aspects of your work. Learn more about our commitment at http://www.kingcounty.gov/equity.

  
  

**Apply now for a rewarding career at the** **Wastewater Treatment Division** **of King County Department of Natural Resources & Parks (DNRP). Join our talented workforce in protecting and restoring the natural environment and promoting more resilient, sustainable, and equitable communities. Enjoy training,** **comprehensive benefits****, and growth opportunities.**

**Job Duties**
--------------

**What You Will Be Doing:**

* Lead Brightwater’s operations, maintenance, and facilities teams through supervisors and technical staff, establishing priorities, setting performance expectations, developing employees, and promoting a safe, inclusive, and accountable work environment.
* Oversee daily treatment operations and facilities maintenance to support reliable service, regulatory compliance, employee safety, and protection of public health and the environment.
* Direct maintenance planning and prioritize preventive and corrective work to improve equipment reliability, address operational risks, and preserve treatment plant assets.
* Participate in the Operations and Maintenance Section Leadership Team, developing and implementing strategic priorities, coordinating across teams, and using performance measures to evaluate results and guide improvements.
* Develop and monitor assigned operating budgets, evaluate staffing and resource needs, and recommend adjustments to support operational priorities and responsible stewardship of public funds.
* Coordinate with engineering, capital project, process, safety, and other support teams to ensure projects and facility changes address operating needs, maintainability, and readiness for service.
* Lead and coordinate the plant’s response to operational disruptions and emergencies in collaboration with section leadership and appropriate support teams.
* Manage employee and labor relations matters in coordination with Human Resources and Labor Relations, including interpreting and applying collective bargaining agreements, conducting fact-finding investigations, resolving conflicts, and recommending appropriate corrective action.

**Experience, Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills**
-------------------------------------------------

**Qualifications You Bring:**

* Experience in leading teams, including team building, building consensus, developing employees, and working effectively with a diverse team.
* Knowledge of the operation and maintenance of wastewater treatment and conveyance systems, including the regulations and requirements as they relate to operation and maintenance of these facilities.
* Knowledge of the principles and practices of engineering and systems operation.
* Knowledge of budget techniques and principles.
* Knowledge of project management principles and techniques.
* Knowledge of labor relations principles, practices, and techniques.
* Skill in writing and communicating technical and non-technical information; skill in reading and interpreting technical information and making presentations to non-technical and technical audiences.
* Knowledge of current and possible future policies, practices, trends, technology, and information affecting the wastewater treatment industry.

  
**Competencies You Bring:**

* **Manages Complexity**: Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
* **Decision Quality**: Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
* **Plans and Aligns**: Planning and prioritizing work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
* **Collaborates**: Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
* **Values Differences**: Recognizing the value that different perspectives and cultures bring to an organization.
* **Builds Effective Teams**: Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspectives to achieve common goals.
* **Communicates Effectively**: Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
* **Drives Engagement**: Creating a climate where people are motivated to do their best to help the organization achieve its objectives.
* **Racially Just**: Identify and replace racist systems and structures with anti-racists and pro-equity approaches.

  
**Required Licenses/Certifications:**

* Washington State Group IV Wastewater Operator’s license (or out-of-state equivalency) or ability to obtain within 6 months.
* Washington State Driver’s License or the ability to provide timely or emergency transportation to work locations with limited or no public transportation.
* Additional licenses, certifications and other requirements determined to be necessary to meet the business needs of the employing unit may be required.
  

  

**It Would Be Great If You Also Bring:**

* Proven ability to lead diverse teams, including union-represented employees.
* Experience aligning operations with organizational goals and environmental sustainability.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including public presentations.
* Experience with performance management, coaching, and workforce development.
* Demonstrated experience with SCADA systems and process automation, preventive and predictive maintenance programs, Regulatory compliance (e.g., NPDES permits, EPA/State reporting, emergency response and disaster preparedness, budget development and capital improvement planning.

  
**Workplace Exposures:**

* The successful candidate will be working within a wastewater treatment plant and potentially exposed to biological hazards, high voltage, equipment that automatically starts and stops, chemicals, loud noise, and other environments typically found in an industrial setting.

**Supplemental Information**
----------------------------

**Working Conditions:**

* **Work Location****:** Brightwater Treatment Plant - 22505 State Route 9 SE, Woodinville, WA 98072.
* **Work Schedule:** This full-time position works a 40-hour work week. This position is exempt from the overtime provision of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) and is not overtime eligible.
* **Union Representation****:** This position is represented by Teamsters 117 - WTD Section and Assistant Managers.

  
**Application Instructions:**
  
We welcome applications from all qualified applicants. We value diversity, diverse perspectives and life experience and encourage people of all backgrounds to apply.
  
  
Application materials will be screened for clarity, completeness and alignment with the experience, qualifications, knowledge, and skills essential for this role to determine which candidates may be invited to participate in a technical assessment and one or more panel interviews.
  
  
**Anticipated** **Timeline for this recruitment (dates subject to change):**

* Technical Assessment: **week of 12/7/26**
* Panel Interview: **week of 12/14/26**

  
To apply, submit a:
  

* **Complete Application**

Note: Additional documents won't be considered during minimum qualification screening.
  
  
**Discover More About the Wastewater Treatment Division**: Visit our **website**and check us out at **Facebook****,** **X (formerly Twitter)****,** **Instagram****,** **YouTube**, and the**WTD Blog****.**
  
  
**Discover More About DNRP: Visit our** **DNRP website****, explore an** **interactive map** **of our recent accomplishments and check us out at** **Facebook****,** **X (formerly Twitter)****,** **LinkedIn****,** **TikTok****,** **Instagram****,** **YouTube** **and** **Keeping King County Green News****.**
  
  
Sign up for Job Alerts to be notified of additional career opportunities with King County. Select the **Natural Resources** category for DNRP opportunities and explore other categories of interest.  
  

Are you ready to make a difference? Come join the team dedicated to serving one of the nation's best places to live, work and play.

**Application Process:**

If you are interested in pursuing this position and supporting King County’s vision for unified, equitable, and high-performing government, please follow the application instructions carefully. Provide us with your work history as applicable, ensuring that you provide details that highlight your ability to fulfill the requirements for this position.

If you need this announcement in an alternate language or format, or you would like to request accommodation or assistance in the application or assessment process, please contact Rodney Dungo at rdungo@kingcounty.gov.

**NOTICE: The posting for local applicants only - is not for those applying for a global assignment and/or for employees working outside of Cipla's U.S. Subsidiaries or Affiliates.**

  

**Job Title**: Senior. Manager, Quality Control

**FLSA Classification**: Full-Time, Exempt Professional

**Work Location**: Central Islip, NY (Unit 3)

**Work Hours:** General Shift: 8:30AM – 5:00PM (may vary based on business needs)

**Reports To**: Quality Control Director

**Salary: $103,000 - $136,000**

  

**Position Summary**

The Manager, Finished Product & Stability Quality Control is responsible for leading all analytical testing, stability program execution, laboratory compliance activities, investigations, and personnel management associated with Finished Product and Stability testing. The role ensures compliance with cGMP, FDA, ICH, USP, Data Integrity, and internal quality requirements while supporting product release, stability commitments, regulatory inspections, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Manage Finished Product and Stability testing activities to support commercial product release and ongoing stability programs.
* Oversee testing and review of assay, related substances, chromatographic purity, degradation products, dissolution, content uniformity, residual solvents, and other compendial requirements.
* Ensure timely execution of stability sample pulls, testing, data review, trending, and reporting activities.
* Lead laboratory investigations including OOS, OOT, deviations, atypical results, and CAPA implementation.
* Review and approve analytical data, laboratory records, chromatograms, and technical reports.
* Support method verification, method transfer, process validation, cleaning validation, and troubleshooting activities.
* Ensure inspection readiness and actively support regulatory and customer audits.
* Supervise, train, mentor, and develop laboratory personnel while ensuring efficient workload distribution and resource utilization.
* Partner with QA, Manufacturing, Validation, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and R&D to meet business and compliance objectives.
  

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or related scientific discipline.
* Minimum 5+ years of pharmaceutical Quality Control experience with at least 3-5 years in a supervisory or managerial role.
* Strong experience supporting FDA-regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.

  

**Technical Knowledge & Competencies**

* Hands-on experience in Finished Product and Stability sample testing within a pharmaceutical Quality Control laboratory. Experience with Raw Material testing is preferred.
* Strong knowledge of chromatographic techniques including assay testing, related substances (impurity profiling), degradation product analysis, and chromatographic purity determination using HPLC, UPLC, GC, and IC systems.
* Proficient in operation, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management of analytical instruments including HPLC, UPLC, GC, IC, Dissolution Testers, Karl Fischer, FTIR, UV-Vis, and XRPD.
* Thorough understanding of Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) product testing requirements and regulatory expectations.
* Strong technical expertise in pharmaceutical analytical methodologies, laboratory investigations, data review, and compliance-driven laboratory operations.
* Working knowledge of cGMP, GLP, GDP, Data Integrity requirements, USP, ICH guidelines, and FDA expectations.
* Experience with chromatography data systems and laboratory software including Empower, LabSolutions, Tiamo, and other computerized laboratory systems.
* Working knowledge of Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), Electronic Laboratory Notebook (ELN), and Quality Management Systems such as TrackWise.
* Demonstrated experience in method execution, method troubleshooting, data review, technical assessments, and investigation management.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and customer audits, including USFDA, customer, and corporate audits.
* Strong leadership, communication, documentation, decision-making, and problem-solving skills with the ability to effectively manage teams and collaborate across functions.

  

**GLOBAL COMPANY**

  

Cipla is a leading global pharmaceutical company, dedicated to high-quality, branded and generic medicines. We are trusted by healthcare professionals and patients across geographies. Over the last eight decades, we have strengthened our leadership in India’s pharmaceutical industry and fortified our promise of strengthening our global focus by consolidating and deepening our presence in the key markets of India, South Africa, the U.S., and other economies of the emerging world.

  

Cipla employs handpicked professionals not just for their knowledge and experience but for their zeal to make a difference to the world of healthcare. The company believes that our biggest assets are the employees, who lead us to prosperity and growth in the future. Driven by the vision, none shall be denied, Cipla’s focus has always been on making affordable, world-class medicines with a reputation for uncompromising quality standards across the world.

  

**CIPLA NEW YORK (INVAGEN PHARMACEUTICALS, INC.)**

  

About InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, a Cipla subsidiary InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is engaged in the development, manufacture, marketing, and distribution of generic prescription medicines with focus on a range of therapeutic areas, including cardiovascular, anti-infective, CNS, anti-inflammatory, anti-diabetic, and anti-depressants. The company was founded in 2003 and is based in Central Islip and Hauppauge, New York. As of February 18, 2016, InvaGen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Cipla (EU) Limited.

**EEO Statement**

Catalent’s Greendale, Indiana site is a key part of the company’s Wellness business, serving as one of North America’s primary gummy development and manufacturing centers. With strong in‑house R&D, quality laboratories, and flexible manufacturing and packaging capabilities, the Greendale operation partners closely with customers to develop innovative, high‑quality, and consumer‑friendly gummy delivery formats across a variety of flavors, shapes, and functional ingredients, all produced under rigorous quality and food‑safety standards.

**Position Summary**
--------------------

We have an opportunity for a Senior Manager, Quality Systems to join our team and lead the Quality and Compliance functions at the Catalent Greendale site. This role oversees a team of Quality Assurance Supervisors and Specialists responsible for operational quality, product sampling, testing, and release. The position ensures compliance with industry standards and regulations while driving continuous improvement across the Quality organization. The successful candidate will collaborate with cross‑functional teams to maintain product integrity and ensure the consistent delivery of high‑quality products to our customers.

Shift: Monday through Friday, 8:00AM - 5:00PM  
Location: Greendale, IN  
100% Onsite

* Lead a team of Quality Assurance Supervisors and Specialists responsible for operational quality, product sampling, testing, and product release.
* Review and approve manufacturing and packaging change controls, product formulations, label changes, deviations, corrective and preventive action plans, and customer complaints.
* Ensure compliance with FDA, NSF, and SQF requirements for product manufacturing and participate in internal and external audits.
* Develop and maintain quality and compliance policies, procedures, and guidelines.

* Support site management in enforcing current Good Manufacturing Practices and mentoring staff in compliance.

**The Candidate**

* Experience communicating with FDA inspectors or other regulatory agents and handling FDA 483 responses.

* Direct complex investigations involving visible particulate matter, inspection trends, and product quality events, driving objective root cause analysis and effective corrective actions.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Laboratory, and Quality teams to identify opportunities for process improvement, defect reduction, and continuous enhancement of inspection performance.
* Support regulatory inspections, customer audits, and health authority interactions by providing expertise, documentation, and responses related to visual inspection and particulate control programs.
* Establish and monitor quality performance metrics, trend analyses, and risk indicators to proactively identify emerging issues and ensure sustainable improvements.

* Experience supporting commercial sterile manufacturing operations for injectable pharmaceutical products.
* Expertise in particulate characterization techniques, defect identification, and contamination control strategies.
* Experience implementing continuous improvement initiatives that improve inspection effectiveness, defect prevention, and process capability.
